items.heading: "Supply Chain Management" "Supply Chain
items.text: "Supply Chain Management" "Supply Chain "Supply Chain Management" "Supply chain management" is a job title that hides five genuinely different daily jobs, ordered below by real growth headroom rather than seniority or how familiar the title sounds. Demand planning leads because every other function runs on its forecast and because planners who add SQL or Python skill routinely earn 30-50% more, the clearest sign this function's ceiling keeps rising as AI-assisted forecasting spreads. Picking the right one, based on which work actually suits you, still matters more than chasing the SCM label itself.

items.heading: Titles Vary By Company
items.text: Titles vary by company and function, but the shape of the climb is consistent across most Indian employers, from e-commerce startups to large manufacturers. Here is what each stage actually looks like, and roughly how long people spend there before moving up.

rows: Typical range for a Supply Chain Analyst or Logistics Coordinator role. Larger companies, GCCs, and graduates from stronger institutes tend to land closer to Rs 6-10 LPA even at entry level.
Executive-level SCM roles, once you can run a vendor category, a delivery zone, or an inventory segment with less supervision.
Manager-level territory across procurement, logistics, and planning. Specialisation, company size, and city meaningfully widen this band.

Senior Manager to Director band. Supply chain manager pay commonly sits around Rs 18-35 LPA; procurement manager roles run Rs 18-30 LPA; logistics director roles can reach Rs 30-50 LPA depending on company scale.
